newsitem.title: UK: Novartis highlights alzheimer, cancer drugs.
newsitem.headline: Novartis highlights alzheimer, cancer drugs.

text.p: Swiss life sciences group Novartis AG highlighted a number of promising drugs in development on Tuesday, including treatments for Alzheimer's disease, cancer, diabetes and irritable bowel syndrome.

In a presentation to a news conference in London following the announcement of 1996 results, Novartis president Daniel Vasella singled out compound NDD094 for its potential in treating Alzheimer's disease and dementia.
Vasella said that in laboratory tests, rats with dementia "were able to learn again" after administration of the drug.

Vasella, who said Novartis had 85 products in clinical development and planned 29 product launches over the next three years, added: "This is the kind of drug that could change and even reverse the effects of dementia."

Another product highlighted was Zelmac for treating Irritable Bowel Syndrome. Vasella said "forty to fifty percent of people being sent from a GP (general practitioner) to a gastro-enterologist have this disturbance.
He said intermediate, or Phase II, trials involving 500 people showed that Zelmac "seems to improve the symptoms and the well-being of the patient, and has substantial potential."
Other development products mentioned included Startrix for diabetes and PSC for cancer.
Vasella said PSC "could be the first drug able to treat people who become resistant to their cancer treatment."
He said the drug had had "encouraging results, for example in ovarian cancer, but there is still work to do." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
